pr.title: Describe the stalled-review notice a draft gets
pr.head: a9abb9cd00b41eaefe4cf2a820fd3771665f43c1

summary: The watch daemon is the one background process per machine that polls the pull requests a session subscribes to and sends the session one-line events, such as NEW HEAD for a head no review has read. Under a repository subscription, which review-repo adds, the daemon announces nothing for a draft until its author marks it ready. One exception already exists in the code: when a review stalls, meaning its lock went unchanged for watch.review_stall seconds, while the pull request is a draft, the daemon sends a single NEW HEAD line that ends stop subagent review-N, and review it once it is ready.

This pull request documents that exception in the two places a session and a reader look for it. The review-pr skill now tells the reviewing session to stop the subagent and start none, because the daemon announces the head again once the draft is ready, and the NEW HEAD row of the events table in docs/cli.md names the exception. The same list in review-pr also corrects its RESPONDED bullet: the event fires only for a head whose newest verdict requests changes.
The change is text only. No code runs differently.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Repository subscription: a session's subscription to every pull request in a repository, as review-repo adds. A subscription to one pull request, as review-pr adds, outranks it and announces every head, draft or not.
  • Stalled review: a review whose lock no project review command touched for watch.review_stall seconds, 30 minutes by default. The daemon clears the lock and tells the owner.
  • RESPONDED: the event that asks for a re-review of an unmoved head after its author answered the findings without pushing.

groups.title: The reviewing session's instructions
groups.kicker: What review-pr tells a session to do on a stalled draft and on RESPONDED
intro: An agent follows skills/review-pr/SKILL.md as instructions, so each bullet in its list of events decides what the session does when that event arrives. Before this change, the bullet for a stalled NEW HEAD said only to stop the subagent and start a new one at once, which is right when the pull request is ready. On a draft under a repository subscription, starting a new subagent would review a head the daemon deliberately holds back until the author is done.

files.note: Adds the draft case to the stalled-review bullet, and rewrites the RESPONDED bullet.

checks.text: The quoted ending matches the draft branch of route_review in src/projector/watch.py word for word, and that branch runs only for a draft whose owning subscription is a repository one (line.number is None). The draft-stall test in tests/test_watch.py asserts the line, a quiet pass after it, and the (still open) reminder once the pull request is ready.
route_review sends RESPONDED only when the newest verdict on the head is changes-requested, and either no review thread is open or the author replied last on an open finding.
The review left one suggestion here: "answered the findings" can read as answering all of them, while one reply on one open finding is enough to fire the event.

groups.title: The events reference
groups.kicker: The NEW HEAD row of the daemon's events table
intro: docs/cli.md lists each event the watch daemon sends, the role that hears it, and what it reports. Its prose under the table already described the stalled-draft line. The table row now names the same exception, so a reader who looks up only the row sees it too.

files.note: Extends the NEW HEAD row with the stalled-draft exception.

checks.text: The daemon sends the line once per stall: it records stalled roles for one polling pass only and clears the stalled lock in that pass.
